issues.detail: Covers mainly the happy path and gives almost no guidance on handling errors such as failed builds, unlinked Git accounts, auth or permission failures, or rollback and cleanup of resources.

scenarios.name: stack-template-with-random-secret
scenarios.rationale: B matches most of the rubric: apiVersion v1.2, a sequential Workflow, refs on every node, ${args.environment}, ${refs.orders-db.id}, ${fn.randomSecret(256)}, `northflank run template --template orders-stack`, and `northflank.json` with `options.autorun: true`. A has no refs, no `${refs...}` usage, uses randomSecret(64), runs the template with a different `--input` form, and gives UI-only Git sync steps with no `northflank.json` or autorun, so it misses most key rubric items.

scenarios.name: scheduled-job-and-migration
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: `--file`, `deployment.docker` customCommand, cron schedule, a manual job with the same body minus `schedule`, `start job run`, and the replica-concurrency reason for keeping migrations out of start. A gets the structure right but uses `--input` instead of `--file`, puts `vcsData` at top level, and only weakly explains why migrations should be manual jobs (it says to remove migrate-on-start, with no mention of multiple replicas).

scenarios.name: ci-login-and-scale-service
scenarios.rationale: Response A matches the rubric's commands: login with `-t "$NORTHFLANK_API_TOKEN" -n ci` from a secret, `scale service --project/--service --input`, `get service logs --tail`, and a note on limiting token permissions. Response B uses `tail service logs` with `--projectId`/`--serviceId` flags, which differ from the rubric, and it only vaguely mentions giving the token a role, with hedging about its own accuracy.
